executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent public health threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) in the Americas represents the highest-priority select agent concern, with ongoing animal-sector detections and pandemic spillover risk warranting Critical-level monitoring. Dengue, mpox, measles, and chikungunya are co-circulating across the Americas with active epidemiological alerts, while the Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset adds additional respiratory burden. Yellow fever activity and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome complete a complex multi-pathogen landscape requiring coordinated regional response.
bottomLine: Multiple simultaneous epidemiological alerts across the Americas — led by H5N1 avian influenza as a BSL-3 select agent threat — indicate an elevated and complex global health security environment as of May 2026.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained H5N1 activity in animal populations
BSL-3 select agent with documented zoonotic spillover potential and pandemic risk
Ongoing circulation in the Americas with alerts spanning multiple months suggesting endemic entrenchment in wild and domestic bird populations
Animal-to-human transmission risk elevated given geographic spread
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces; ensure antiviral stockpile readiness; coordinate with USDA and national veterinary authorities; consider risk communication to exposed occupational groups

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating significant regional activity
Historical pattern of early-year surges in tropical Americas consistent with ongoing transmission
Multiple serotype co-circulation increases severe disease and secondary infection risk
Alert issued during peak transmission season for the Southern Hemisphere
threats.action: Strengthen vector surveillance and control; ensure hospital surge capacity for severe dengue; promote community-level Aedes aegypti elimination; monitor serotype shifts for DHF/DSS risk

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 confirming ongoing transmission in the Americas
BSL-3 select agent with person-to-person transmission and emerging clade concerns
Sustained multi-country circulation following 2022-2023 outbreak suggesting endemic establishment
April 2026 update indicates continued need for surveillance and response measures
threats.action: Maintain mpox vaccination programs for high-risk populations; enhance genomic surveillance to detect clade II vs clade I introductions; ensure diagnostic capacity at national reference laboratories; review contact tracing protocols

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active risk in the Americas
BSL-3 select agent with high case fatality rate in unvaccinated populations
Epizootic activity in non-human primates typically precedes human spillover events
Alert timing suggests active sylvatic cycle expansion
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations and travelers; expand epizootic surveillance in non-human primates; ensure yellow fever vaccine availability; issue travel health advisories for endemic zones

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating transmission risk in the Americas
Ongoing global resurgence linked to COVID-19 pandemic-era vaccination gaps
Americas Region had achieved elimination status making any re-introduction a public health emergency
Alert suggests importation or endemic re-establishment requiring urgent vaccination response
threats.action: Conduct urgent vaccination coverage assessments; implement supplementary immunization activities in low-coverage areas; activate outbreak investigation protocols for any confirmed case; strengthen port-of-entry surveillance

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained and increasing activity
Dual alerts within three months suggest waning immunity cycle and possible resurgence
Infant and unvaccinated populations at highest risk for severe outcomes
Global pertussis resurgence pattern consistent with regional trend
threats.action: Review Tdap booster coverage in adolescents and adults; strengthen maternal vaccination programs; ensure diagnostic capacity for laboratory confirmation; monitor for AMR in Bordetella pertussis

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025 indicating cases of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome
High case fatality rate (30-40%) with no specific antiviral treatment
Rodent reservoir dynamics influenced by climate and seasonal patterns
Andes virus strain has documented person-to-person transmission capability in South America
threats.action: Enhance rodent surveillance and control in endemic areas; conduct risk communication for rural and occupationally exposed populations; ensure ICU capacity for severe respiratory cases; investigate any clustering for Andes virus person-to-person transmission

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission
Co-circulation with dengue and Zika complicates clinical diagnosis and surveillance
Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus vectors widespread across the Americas enabling rapid spread
Potential for explosive urban outbreaks in naive or low-immunity populations
threats.action: Integrate chikungunya diagnostics into arboviral surveillance platforms; enhance Aedes vector control; train clinicians on differential diagnosis from dengue; monitor for geographic expansion into previously unaffected areas

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents and one BSL-3 pathogen of concern have been identified in this surveillance cycle. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — a Tier 1 select agent — has generated two PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025, March 2026) for the Americas, indicating sustained zoonotic risk with pandemic spillover potential; this represents the highest-priority biosecurity concern. Mpox virus (MPXV), a BSL-3 select agent, is under active PAHO surveillance as of April 2026 with ongoing transmission in the Americas. Yellow fever virus, a BSL-3 pathogen, has triggered a March 2026 PAHO alert suggesting active sylvatic cycle activity. All three require enhanced laboratory biosafety protocols, genomic surveillance, and coordination with national biosecurity authorities.

amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis: Dual alerts in 3-month period warrants monitoring for macrolide resistance emergence given increased antibiotic use during outbreaks
Seasonal Influenza: Antiviral resistance (oseltamivir) monitoring critical given simultaneous H5N1 zoonotic pressure and seasonal co-circulation — dual antiviral use increases selection pressure
General AMR concern: Co-circulation of multiple bacterial and viral pathogens increases empiric antibiotic use, elevating broader AMR selection pressure across the Americas
emergingPatterns: Multi-pathogen co-circulation burden: Simultaneous PAHO alerts for dengue, chikungunya, measles, mpox, yellow fever, hantavirus, pertussis, and H5N1 in the Americas suggests healthcare system stress and diagnostic capacity strain
Southern Hemisphere respiratory season onset (April 2026) coincides with active circulation of mpox and arboviral diseases, creating compounding clinical presentation challenges
Sustained H5N1 activity across two separate multi-month reporting periods (Nov 2025 and Mar 2026) suggests entrenchment in Americas animal reservoirs beyond seasonal epizootic patterns
Resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) indicates persistent vaccination coverage gaps likely attributable to pandemic-era disruption of routine immunization programs
Dual alerts for pertussis within 3 months (Dec 2025, Mar 2026) consistent with global pertussis resurgence cycle and may signal waning immunity in previously vaccinated cohorts
ECDC issuing weekly communicable disease threat reports through Weeks 16-20 of 2026 indicates sustained European surveillance engagement with active multi-threat monitoring

GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert (Feb 2026) and methanol poisoning alert (Oct 2025) highlight non-infectious public health threats competing for response resources alongside biological threats

Convergence of zoonotic threats (H5N1, hantavirus, yellow fever) with vector-borne and vaccine-preventable disease resurgence represents a complex One Health emergency requiring integrated human-animal-environment surveillance
